Chapter 3: The Role of Beliefs and the Nature of Resistance
Now that we’ve explored the Law of Attraction and how your emotions guide you, let’s dive into the world of beliefs—and why they matter so much.
Think of beliefs as thoughts you’ve repeated so many times, they just feel true. They’re like invisible filters, coloring what you notice and shaping how you experience the world.
Some beliefs open up new doors and possibilities—you know that feeling when you’re sure you can do something, and suddenly, opportunities seem to pop up everywhere? That’s an empowering belief at work.
But beliefs can also quietly close doors behind you. Imagine someone who’s convinced opportunities are scarce. Even if a great chance comes along, they might not even see it.
On the other hand, if you believe the world is full of abundance, you’re more likely to spot those chances and actually do something about them.
So, what happens when you want something, but your beliefs don’t line up with that desire? That’s where resistance comes in.
Picture this: you’re dreaming of traveling the world, but deep down, you hold onto the thought that travel is too dangerous or just too expensive.
Your desire is pulling you one way, but your belief tugs you the other. That push and pull creates emotional tension—a kind of inner friction we call resistance. And resistance? It’s like trying to drive with the parking brake on. It slows you down, maybe even stops you from moving forward at all.
Here’s something a lot of people get wrong: letting go of resistance isn’t about forcing yourself to change your mind all at once. Instead, it’s a gentle process. It starts by questioning those limiting beliefs—just a little.
Maybe you notice a moment when your belief doesn’t quite match up with what’s actually happening. Or you try imagining how it would feel to believe something a bit more supportive.
I love this metaphor: think of your desires as a river, always flowing toward what you want. Resistance? That’s like rowing your boat upstream—hard work, right? But if you let go of that resistance, it’s like turning your boat around. Suddenly, you’re moving with the current, and it all feels so much easier.
So, how do you actually release resistance in everyday life?
Here are a few simple practices you can try:
First, pay attention to your thoughts. If something feels heavy or discouraging, that’s usually resistance showing up. It’s a signal worth noticing.
Next, gently challenge those limiting beliefs. Ask yourself, “Is this always true?” or “Could there be another way to look at this?” Just opening the door to a new possibility can make a difference.
And finally, try focusing on the parts of a situation that feel even a little bit better. Sometimes, just a tiny shift in perspective is all it takes to get momentum moving in a more positive direction.
Remember, the journey to releasing resistance isn’t about perfection—it’s about noticing, gently questioning, and letting yourself drift more easily with the current of your own desires.
